title: Advanced Mensuration — 3D Solids
tagline: Year 3 — Volume and surface area of cubes, cuboids, cylinders, cones, spheres, melting and recasting

introduction.overview: Solid shapes are measured by volume (space inside) and surface area (outer covering). This chapter covers cubes, cuboids, cylinders, cones, spheres and hemispheres, the slant height of a cone, and the idea that melting one solid and recasting it into another keeps the volume unchanged. Water-flow and painting-cost questions are built on the same formulas.
introduction.placementRelevance: Volume and surface-area questions are staples of aptitude papers, usually as melting-and-recasting or cost-of-painting problems.
introduction.realWorldContext: Tank capacity, packaging, pipe flow and material costing all depend on solid measures.

learningObjectives: Recall volume and surface area formulas
Compute the slant height of a cone
Find the number of smaller solids from a bigger one
Calculate costs of painting and filling

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Volume is measured in cubic units, area in square units. Use π = 22/7 unless a calculator value is given.

coreDefinitions: Cube of side a: volume a³, total surface area 6a², diagonal a√3.
Cuboid l × b × h: volume lbh, surface area 2(lb + bh + hl), diagonal √(l² + b² + h²).
Cylinder: volume πr²h, curved area 2πrh, total area 2πr(r + h).
Cone: volume ⅓πr²h, slant height l = √(r² + h²), curved area πrl, total area πr(r + l).
Sphere: volume 4/3 πr³, area 4πr². Hemisphere: volume 2/3 πr³, total area 3πr².
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Volume scales with the cube of the length and area with the square. Doubling the radius of a sphere multiplies its volume by 8 and its surface by 4.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Write the formula, put the numbers in, and cancel π and 7 before multiplying. For recasting, equate the volumes and cancel π.

mainNarrative: A cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm has volume (22/7) × 49 × 10 = 1540 cm³ and curved surface area 2 × (22/7) × 7 × 10 = 440 cm².
A cone of radius 6 cm and height 8 cm has slant height √(36 + 64) = 10 cm, curved area (22/7) × 6 × 10 ≈ 188.6 cm², and volume ⅓ × (22/7) × 36 × 8 ≈ 301.7 cm³.
Melting and recasting keep the volume equal. A solid sphere of radius 6 cm is melted into small spheres of radius 2 cm. The number is (6/2)³ = 27.
A cube of side 6 cm is cut into cubes of side 2 cm. The number of small cubes is (6/2)³ = 27, and the total surface area increases from 216 cm² to 27 × 24 = 648 cm².
When a solid is scaled by k, its surface area multiplies by k² and its volume by k³. If the radius of a sphere increases by 50% the volume becomes (3/2)³ = 27/8 of the original, a rise of 237.5%.

deepDiveAspects.title: Water flow
deepDiveAspects.content: Volume per minute = cross-section area × speed. A pipe of radius 7 cm with water at 5 m/s delivers π × 49 × 500 cm³ per second.

solvedExamples.title: Recasting
solvedExamples.question: A solid metallic sphere of radius 6 cm is melted and recast into small spheres of radius 2 cm. How many spheres are formed?
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The ratio of radii is 3, so the ratio of volumes is 27.

solvedExamples.title: Cone
solvedExamples.question: A cone has base radius 6 cm and height 8 cm. Find its slant height and volume (use π = 22/7).
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: Cone volume is a third of the cylinder of the same base and height.
solvedExamples.commonTrap: Using the slant height as h.

solvedExamples.title: Painting cost
solvedExamples.question: A cuboid is 5 m long, 4 m wide and 3 m high. What does it cost to paint its four walls at ₹10 per m²?

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Equate volumes, cancel π and common factors, then take cube roots or ratios.

commonMistakes.mistake: Adding floor and ceiling to wall area

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Volume answers scale by the cube of the length ratio.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Use 22/7 only when radii are multiples of 7.
